## Historical audit — S0119

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r2/sceneevolve_cli/C1/test/commons_199974832/trajectory.jsonl`. This audit covers only the supplied chunk 2 of 3; the referenced images are not visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observation and limits |
|---|---|
| Line 15, student `model_request`, chars [0,234054) | The instructed goal was an editable, photograph-matched indoor scene with separate meshes, camera and materials. The student interpreted it as a woodworking tool room; that semantic identification and its image-anchor comments are student inferences, not independent verification. |
| Line 15, same event | The first program creates multiple architecture, shelf, bench and tool assets, including composite plane bodies, blades and handles. It assigns wood, iron and glass-like colors, procedural wood bump and metallic settings; it sets object rotations, a camera and two lights. Grouping and coordinates demonstrate intended part relationships, not verified physical connections or accurate poses. |
| Line 15, same event | The harness reports successful steps 1 and 2 and supplies render paths. After step 1 the student described the render as too pale, the squares too small and low, and the foreground too sparse and low. The second program darkened materials and lighting, stretched the wall-tool group, raised and populated the bench, and changed lens 32 to 33. These are student diagnoses and code changes, not independently observed image discrepancies. |
| Lines 16–18, `codex_session`, `model_response`, `execute`, chars [0,3828), [0,14094), [0,14743) respectively | In a fresh read-only session with shell, browsing and other tools disabled, the student received the reference and two render attachments. It reported squares still too narrow, rows too uniform and foreground too clean and pale. Its third program widened square components, varied plane dimensions and angles, added tools, and further darkened finishes and ambient light. The execution event records that program being run. The session records zero tool calls; this is iterative student exploration through supplied renders, not external exploration. |
| Lines 19–21, `execution_result` and two `select` events, chars [0,129175), [0,59), [0,59) | Step 3 reports `ok: true`, a completed render, saved scene and image, and empty stderr; step 3 is selected twice. This establishes **formal execution/render success**, not visual or geometric correctness. No empty patch, algorithm failure or technical interruption is visible here. Overall reconstruction quality and final outcome beyond the selection remain unknown. |

**Teacher input and adoption:** No distinct teacher message, teacher detection, diagnosis or proposed update is visible in this chunk. The harness supplied procedural instructions and render feedback; the revisions visibly follow the student’s own stated diagnoses. No teacher receipt or adoption can be established from availability elsewhere.

**Lessons and uncertainty:** The transferable pattern is to separate render success from image-match evidence and to track proposed corrections through execution. The particular darkening, square widening and crowded bench are scene-specific hypotheses. Without the images or other chunks, whether the camera, lighting, textures, object placement, occlusion, part connections and poses match the photograph—and whether the revisions improved them—remains unresolved.
